This is a summary report of the Baobabs in Africa Mapped (BAM) Project dataset, produced after undergoing Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) checks. The purpose is
to vusualise the dataset.

```{r, results = 'asis', echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

#| label: Setup


# Load the required packages

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(knitr)
library(writexl)
library(janitor)
library(WorldFlora)
library(fuzzyjoin)
library(patchwork)

```



The dataset contains `r n_observations` individual tree observations; among them, `r n_baobabs` were baobabs and `r n_non_baobabs` were non-baobab trees .  
The dataset was contributed by `r length_contributors_list` people (`r contributors_list`).  
There are `r length_countries` countries (`r country_list`).

```{r, results = 'asis', echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

#| label: Map-of-Africa

# Loading the map of Africa, which we shall use for checking the coordinates, 
# if they fall within the continent of Africa.

# Get the Africa map

africa_one <- ne_countries(continent = "Africa", returnclass = "sf")

# Convert the CRS to match the data frames.

sf_use_s2(FALSE)

africa <- ne_countries(continent = "Africa", returnclass = "sf") |> 
  st_union() |> 
  st_as_sf()

```




```{r, results = 'asis', echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

# Define the custom theme

theme_fancy <- function() {
  theme_bw() +
    theme(
      text = element_text(family = "Helvetica"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
      axis.line.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.5, color = "black"),
      axis.line.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.5, color = "black"),
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, color = "black"),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "cm"),
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 10,
        vjust = 1,
        hjust = 0.5,
        color = "black"
      ),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      legend.position = "bottom", #c(0.9, 0.9),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.9, "line"),
      legend.background = element_rect(
        color = "black",
        fill = "transparent",
        linewidth = 2,
        linetype = "blank"
      )
    )
}
windowsFonts("Helvetica" = windowsFont("Helvetica")) # Ensure font is mapped correctly

```


We plotted the girth probability density distribution curves for the dataset (Figure 1). The Non-Baobab trees shows a high peaks at smaller girths, between 1 and 2 metres, indicating that most of these trees have relatively slender trunks. Non-Baobab trees display a sharper peak near the smallest canopy sizes, which means that a greater proportion of these trees in the dataset have a small limited canopy spread. In contrast, baobab trees have shown a broader distribution, with few small-girthed individuals and a substantial proportion extending into larger girth categories, some trees are exceeding 16 metres. The overlap between the two distributions at lower girth values indicates some similarity in smaller sized trees, yet the divergence at larger sizes could be explained by the fact that most baobabs have massive trunks within African landscapes.


```{r, results = 'asis', echo = FALSE, out.height = "40%", out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Girth probability density distribution", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

#| label: fig-girth-density
#.............plot tree girth
# Density plot with normalized probabilities for tree girth
Plot_girth_BAM <- ggplot(bam_csv, aes(x = stem_one_cir / 100, 
                                      fill = Tree_type, 
                                      color = Tree_type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 0.6) +
  labs(
    x = "Girth (m)",
    y = "Probability Density",
    fill = "Tree Type",  
    color = "Tree Type"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 35, by = 5), 
    limits = c(0, 35)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Non-Baobab" = "skyblue", "Baobab" = "darkblue")) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Non-Baobab" = "skyblue", "Baobab" = "darkblue")) +  
  theme_fancy() 
Plot_girth_BAM
#Save the plot with A4 dimensions at 600 DPI
ggsave(
  filename = "C:/Workspace/Baobabs_in_Africa_Mapped/Data/outputs/Plots/Plot_girth_BAM.png",
  plot = Plot_girth_BAM, 
  width = 21.0,    # A4 width in cm
  height = 14.85,   # A4 height in cm (landscape)
  units = "cm",
  dpi = 600
)


```

We plotted the canopy areas probability density distribution curves for the dataset (Figure 2). Both baobab and non-baobab have exhibited small canopy areas, with canopy areas peaking below 2 m². Non-Baobab trees shows a sharper peak near the smallest canopy sizes, which means that a greater proportion of these trees in the dataset have a small limited canopy spread. However, Baobab trees have shown a broader distribution with a heavier right tail, indicating the presence of some individuals with substantially larger canopies, extending beyond 6 m² and, in rare cases, exceeding 16 m². The differences in canopy growth characteristics between the two groups, can potentially be linked to species-specific morphology, ecological settings and environmental conditions across the surveyed regions.


```{r, results = 'asis', echo = FALSE, out.height = "40%", out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Canopy areas probability density distribution", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

#| label: fig-canopy-density

# Calculate canopy areas for all trees
BAM_canopy_areas <- bam_csv |>
  mutate(
    canopy_areas = pi * (ns_crown_width / 2) * (ew_crown_width / 2)
  )

# Density plot for canopy areas
Plot_BAM_canopies <- ggplot(BAM_canopy_areas, aes(x = canopy_areas, 
                                                   fill = Tree_type, 
                                                   color = Tree_type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 0.6) +
  labs(
    x = "Canopy Area (sq. meters)",
    y = "Probability Density",
    fill = "Tree Type",  
    color = "Tree Type"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 700, by = 100), 
    limits = c(0, 700)
  ) +
  #scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Non-Baobab" = "skyblue", "Baobab" = "darkblue")) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Non-Baobab" = "skyblue", "Baobab" = "darkblue")) +  
  theme_fancy() 

Plot_BAM_canopies

# Save the plot with A4 dimensions at 600 DPI
ggsave(
  filename = "C:/Workspace/Baobabs_in_Africa_Mapped/Data/outputs/Plots/Plot_BAM_canopies.png",
  plot = Plot_BAM_canopies, 
  width = 21.0,    # A4 width in cm
  height = 14.85,   # A4 height in cm (landscape)
  units = "cm",
  dpi = 600
)


```



To understand the distribution of species in our dataset, we plotted a histogram (Figure 3). The species frequency distribution reveals a highly uneven pattern, characterised by a Unknown species (species that were not identified by contributors). This skewed distribution was expected, given the variation in data sources across contributors. However, despite this variability, the dataset provides valuable insights, which are essential for subsequent analyses.

```{r, results = 'asis', echo = FALSE, out.height = "40%", out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Non-baobab species distribution", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

#| label: fig-species-distribution

# Filter and prepare Non-Baobab species data
species_data <- bam_csv |>
  filter(Tree_type == "Non-Baobab") |>
  mutate(scientificName = replace_na(scientificName, "Unknown"))

# Create species distribution plot in portrait orientation
plot_species_distribution <- ggplot(species_data, aes(x = fct_rev(fct_infreq(scientificName)))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "skyblue", color = "grey30", width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Species",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_flip() +  # Rotate to portrait orientation
  #scale_x_log10() +
  theme_fancy() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "italic", color = "black"),  # Species names in italics
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "plain", color = "black"),
    #panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )

plot_species_distribution

# Save the plot at half A4 width, full height
ggsave(
  filename = "C:/Workspace/Baobabs_in_Africa_Mapped/Data/outputs/Plots/plot_species_distribution_rotated.png",
  plot = plot_species_distribution, 
  width = 21.0,     # Full A4 width in cm
  height = 29.7,    # Full A4 height in cm (portrait)
  units = "cm",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)


```

To understand the spatial distribution of tree data collection across Africa, the geographic locations of tree observations are plotted as individual points on the map (Figure 4), showing where each tree was recorded across the continent. The tree locations are displayed at a coarser scale to enhance visual clarity.


```{r, fig.cap = "Geographic Locations of Tree Observations", results = 'asis', echo = FALSE, out.height = "40%", out.width = "100%", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

#| label: Map

# Convert bam_data to sf object

clean_data_sf <- bam_csv |> 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# Plot map with observation points

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = africa_one, color = "black") +
  geom_sf(data = clean_data_sf, 
          color = "darkgreen", size = 0.4, alpha = 0.6) +
  coord_sf(lims_method = "geometry_bbox") + 
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank()
  )

```



```{r, results = 'asis', echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

#| label: Map for the webpage
# Create outer boundary of Africa
#| label: fig-webpage-map

# Create outer boundary of Africa

africa_outline <- africa_one |> 
  st_union() |>       
  st_as_sf()

# Convert observation points to sf object

clean_data_sf <- bam_csv |> 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# Create map for webpage

map_for_webpage <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = africa_one, color = "grey60", fill = "grey95", linewidth = 0.2) +   
  geom_sf(data = clean_data_sf, color = "darkgreen", size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +  
  geom_sf(data = africa_outline, color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.2) +     
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
  )

map_for_webpage

# Save with timestamped filename and transparent background

timestamp <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S")
filename  <- file.path("C:/Workspace/Baobabs_in_Africa_Mapped/Data/outputs/Plots",
                       paste0("webpage_map_", timestamp, ".png"))

ggsave(
  filename = filename,
  plot     = map_for_webpage, 
  width    = 21.0,
  height   = 14.85,
  units    = "cm",
  dpi      = 600,
  bg       = "transparent"
)

```
